frontier.hypothesis: FR1 (terminal) — motion_Close is a fully determined ESCALATION candidate awaiting the driver's routing; there is no C-side probe left to run.
frontier.mechanism: Floor flat at 13 for EIGHT sessions across six modalities. The 13 residual points are paired instruction-by-instruction (s7 residual_table.md, verified against the current chassis in s10 and re-verified against the new session-12 form) and all three mechanisms carry backend-level disproofs: H1 (REG_PARM_STACK_SPACE is the compile-time constant 16 applied by MAX on every call-expansion path — mips.h:1822, calls.c:1245/1400, mips.c:4466; the only cfoas-free site, __builtin_apply, emits a frame pointer, a 72-byte frame and 34 insns), F5 (ascending first-free hard-reg scan, no MIPS REG_ALLOC_ORDER, so $v0 is never $t0), F7a (mips.c:4680 emits GP saves high-to-low unconditionally) and F7b (an empty beqz delay slot needs a block with no eligible single insn while the target's holds four; 0/1788 compiled-C counterexamples). SIX input axes outside the walk are measured dead — F10 whole-TU, F11 declarations, F12 loop construct, F13 guard/materialisation shape, F14 wrap placement, and the dead-store substitution.
frontier.next_probe: None on the C side; do NOT re-measure a dead axis. When the driver assigns `escalation` modality, the packet is already written and both endgame-lock gates FAIL, so under the owner's 2026-07-27 standing auto-ruling the terminal entry is `OWNER-ESCALATION — RESOLVED BY STANDING RULING (2026-07-27): REFUSED / OWNER-ACCEPTED INCOMPLETE`, citing the s7 backend disproof of H1, the s7 residual table, the s5b scan-order disproof of F5, the s6 corpus disproofs of F7a/F7b, the s6 scan_hand_coded LOW tier, and the s8–s12 quintet showing every input to cc1 outside the walk itself is inert. Note the packet must now describe the SINGLE-level in-walk form, not the two-level initialiser form.

frontier.hypothesis: FR2 (CLOSED at its floor by session 12) — the policy device cannot be made lighter than one do-while(0) level.
frontier.mechanism: Session 12 met FR2's criterion (13 at wrap depth <= 1) by moving the note's PLACEMENT onto p's `p++` bump, where it is worth two weighted references per level instead of the initialiser's one, and paying for the resulting schedule fence with a free statement reorder (`count--` ahead of `f()`). Depth 0 is then derived unreachable from the measured constants (p 4/8 = 10000 vs count 5/7 = 14285): the three routes to a flip each need instructions the target lacks.
frontier.next_probe: None. Do not re-open the device-weight axis; the remaining device is one non-nested do-while(0) with an inline FAKE annotation, inside the frozen sanctioned family, and prerequisite 3 no longer applies. If a future session wants a device-free form it must first invalidate one of the three depth-0 routes above, which requires a p-reference or an intervening computation present in the TARGET's 26 instructions — s7's residual table says there is none.

frontier.hypothesis: FR3 (housekeeping) — keep the escalation packet true to whatever form candidate.c actually holds.
frontier.mechanism: Twice before, the ledger's authoritative residual analysis was derived on a chassis a later session superseded; equal scores do not imply equal residual composition. Session 12 DID change candidate.c, so it discharged the obligation in-session: the new form's cc1 stream was diffed against tmp/grind/motion_Close/s10/f12_G_goto_tail_d2.s and is identical but for the internal label number, so the s7 table still applies.
frontier.next_probe: Unchanged for future sessions: any session that changes candidate.c must re-emit the build stream from the instrumented cc1 and diff it against tmp/grind/motion_Close/s10/f12_G_goto_tail_d2.s (or s5b/wsA/_base.txt, which is a byte/reloc dump, not cc1 asm — use the s10 file for a text diff) before reusing the s7 residual table.
